fields.rationale: States cluster by their dominant requirement emphasis: some center on verified years of active practice, some on good-standing equivalency alone, some layer on substantial credential and exam hurdles, some reference specific compact or portability frameworks, one prohibits true reciprocity, and a few impose only minimal conditions.

assignments.raw_value: Applicant must meet qualifications of AS 08.36.110, submit proof of continued competence, pay fees, and hold an active license from another state or territory or have passed an examination specified by the board. In-person interview with the board or a board member is required before issuance.

Applicant must have been actively practicing for 5 years or 5,000 hours, hold a current valid license in a state with equivalent examination standards, be in good standing without restrictions, pass a written jurisprudence examination, submit affidavits from two licensed dentists, and satisfy other board criteria.

Applicant must have practiced continuously for at least 5 years under a license lawfully issued by another state, territory, DC, or Canada where the standard of proficiency at least equals that of Arkansas. Application must include fee, original or certified copy of license, and certificate from issuing authority. Board has discretion to issue license.

Licensure by credential available; board may waive clinical exam if passed in another state more than 5 years prior, with substantially equivalent standards, minimum active practice hours, and completion of CE requirements in the prior jurisdiction. Fee not more than $2,000.

Applicant must hold an active, unrestricted license from another US state/territory; must have been in active clinical practice for at least five years immediately preceding the application (or meet alternative service commitment criteria); must not have been subject to disciplinary action; must submit 50 units of CE completed within two years; must pass California law and ethics exam.

Applicant must satisfy the requirements of the occupational credential portability program (substantially equivalent experience or credentials, good standing in another state, payment of fees, and compliance with other applicable requirements).

Applicant must hold a current valid license in good professional standing from another state or territory with standards commensurate with Connecticut's (except for practical examination), have worked continuously as a licensed dentist in an academic or clinical setting for at least one year immediately preceding the application, have no pending disciplinary action or unresolved complaint, and pay a fee of $565.

Applicant must present proof of current licensure in good standing in another state/DC/territory; for dentists: CODA-accredited dental degree, 3 years of active dental practice in another jurisdiction, and meet other § 1122 requirements; for dental hygienists: 3 of last 5 years practice, passage of NBDE and jurisprudence exams; all must have valid CPR certification and remain academically current.

MOBILE Act (Mobile Opportunity by Interstate Licensure Endorsement Act): applicant must hold active, unencumbered license from another state with similar scope of practice, have actively practiced at least 2 years in the preceding 4 years, pass a national licensure examination or hold recognized national certification, have no pending disciplinary proceedings, and no disciplinary action in the preceding 5 years. Florida also accepts ADLEX scores from other jurisdictions after October 1, 2011, subject to conditions in s. 466.006(4)(b).

Provisional license by credentials requires DDS or DMD from CODA-accredited school, five years full-time clinical practice or faculty (or combination), active dental license in good standing from another state, passage of board-approved clinical examination and jurisprudence examination.

Licensure by endorsement available for nonresident military spouses and under general reciprocity provisions; applicant must hold current active license from another jurisdiction meeting equivalency standards.

License by credentials available without examination if applicant holds equivalent license from another state and has either passed a regional or national examination approved by the dental board or has been in legal practice for three consecutive years immediately prior to application.

Active license in good standing in another state; at least 5 years and 3,500 hours of clinical practice; graduated from CODA-accredited dental school; passed national board dental examinations; passed board-approved clinical examination; paid application fee.

Applicant must have been lawfully licensed in another state or territory with standards at least equal to Illinois, must have been lawfully engaged in practice for at least 2 years immediately preceding application, must deposit a duly attested certificate from the Board of the other state certifying licensure and good moral character, and pay the required fee. 'Substantially equivalent' means graduation from an ADA-accredited dental college, passing both parts of the National Board Dental Examination, and successful completion of a regional testing service examination.

Must be licensed in another state or province of Canada with substantially equal requirements, practiced dentistry for at least 2 of the 3 preceding years, pass the law examination, complete required CE hours in previous 2 years, and meet all other requirements.

Applicant must have held a license in another state for 5 years, engaged in active practice for 5 years, passed a national board exam and clinical exam, met continuing education requirements, and have no disciplinary history.
Requirements for reciprocity are set by administrative regulation.
Reciprocity is prohibited; licensure by credentials is available for dentists holding a dental license in another state.

Applicant must have been lawfully in practice for at least 5 years in another state, present a certificate of registration and duration of practice from that state's board, and the other state must require a degree of competency equal to that required in Massachusetts.

Applicant must have passed the ADLEX and Maryland Dental Jurisprudence Examination, OR have been actively practicing dentistry for at least 850 hours/year for the preceding 5 years, passed an exam with a clinical component in another state, passed a comprehensive written ADEX exam, and passed the Maryland Dental Jurisprudence Examination. Must meet all other qualifications for a general license, hold a license in another state, not be under investigation or disciplined, and not have previously failed a Maryland licensure exam.

Applicant must be licensed in good standing in another jurisdiction; may qualify by showing 3 consecutive years of substantially equivalent licensure or by showing substantially similar qualifications; must comply with section 18341 general requirements.

Applicant must substantially meet the requirements of Michigan law and rules for licensure, and must be licensed in another state or province of Canada that maintains standards substantially equivalent to Michigan's.

Applicant must have passed all components of the National Board Dental Examinations, been in active practice at least 2,000 hours within 36 months, hold or have held a license in another state or Canadian province in good standing, be of good moral character, and meet other credentialing requirements specified by board rule. Interstate compact also available.

Licensed in another state for at least 5 consecutive years immediately preceding application; qualifications at least equivalent to Missouri initial registration requirements; at least 21 years of age; good moral character. Board may require Missouri law exam and/or practical exam if licensure in any state was denied, revoked, or suspended for incompetency, or if applicant failed a practical exam.

Licensure by credentials requires: ADA-accredited school graduation, active practice for past 5 years, valid unrestricted license in a reciprocal state, no pending or final disciplinary action, passed a state or regional clinical licensure exam, completed National Board Examinations, passed a written jurisprudence examination, and payment of application fee.

Applicant must be licensed in another state with substantially equivalent standards, affirm that verification has been requested from the other state, and have no pending charges or final disciplinary action for unprofessional conduct or impairment.

Applicant must have DDS or DMD from CODA-accredited program, good moral character, five years of active practice, no disciplinary action, no failed NC Board examination, and must pass Jurisprudence and Sterilization and Infection Control examinations. Border-state applicants (bordering NC) receive mandatory licensure by credentials under a reciprocal arrangement.

Applicant must have been licensed in good standing and actively practicing dentistry in another jurisdiction for at least five years immediately preceding application where requirements are substantially equivalent; must pay fee; deliver certificates of good standing from all licensing jurisdictions; pass ND laws and rules examination; meet any additional requirements established by board rule.

Must meet standards set by the board and have been actively engaged in the practice of dentistry for at least one year under a license in another state or territory of the United States or the District of Columbia. Practice in an accredited school or college of dentistry for the purpose of completing a postgraduate or residency program also counts toward this requirement.
Requirements or standards for licensure in the other state must be equivalent to or greater than New Hampshire's; board posts list of qualifying states and terms for licensure by endorsement.

Applicant must have been licensed in another state or foreign country and practiced dentistry for at least five years immediately preceding application; must present proof by affidavit; must present a certificate from the dental board of the other state certifying competency and good moral character, presented within six months of its date; and the other state must recognize New Jersey certificates in like manner.

Expedited license (without examination) available to dentists licensed in another jurisdiction with a current, good-standing license. Board may also issue a general license by credentials to applicants licensed by clinical examination in another state/territory with all licenses in good standing for five years, no board actions, and no pending proceedings. Applicant must pass NM laws/rules exam.

Must hold a valid and unrestricted license in another state/territory; have no disciplinary history; have no revocations or refusals; pay applicable fees; submit fingerprints; satisfy other requirements of NRS 622.530.

Applicant must file an application, meet educational requirements, have satisfactory experience, pass an examination satisfactory to the board, be at least 21, be a US citizen or lawfully admitted noncitizen, and be of good moral character. The board of regents may also evaluate prior disciplinary history from other jurisdictions.

Applicant must hold a license to practice dentistry in another state, or have satisfactory work experience, government certification, or private certification in a state that does not issue such a license. Jurisprudence examination may be required. Ohio also participates in the Dentist and Dental Hygienist Compact for compact privilege.

Dentist must hold a general dentist license in good standing, have practiced at least 500 hours within the previous 5 years, and have passed a regional examination substantially equivalent to Oklahoma requirements. Must also pass the jurisprudence examination and provide a letter of good standing from all states in which ever licensed.

Applicant must have engaged in active practice for at least 3,500 hours in the five years immediately preceding application and meet all other requirements for licensure. Board accepts results of regional and national testing agencies or clinical board examinations from other states.
Standards of the other state, territory, or Canada must be equal to Pennsylvania's standards, and that jurisdiction must reciprocally recognize Pennsylvania licenses
Available for military members and spouses licensed in another state for at least one year, where requirements of the other state are substantially equivalent to Rhode Island's.

Reciprocity available to licensees of other states who are members of regional testing services of which the board is a member. License by credentials also available upon meeting requirements including 5 years active practice, 70 CE hours over past 5 years, clean disciplinary history, jurisprudence exam, and other conditions.

Applicant must hold a valid license in another state with requirements the same as or higher than South Dakota's; must have graduated from a CODA-accredited U.S. dental school with a DMD or DDS; must have completed at least 3,000 dental clinical hours within the preceding five years; must have passed a national comprehensive exam and a clinical regional or national exam approved by the board; must have passed the SD laws and rules exam; no pending disciplinary proceedings; and must provide references of good moral character.

Applicant must currently hold a valid license in another state; no pending disciplinary charges; not failed a TN licensure examination previously; graduated from CODA-accredited dental school; demonstrates intent to practice or teach in TN; has practiced or taught for at least 2-5 years (depending on pathway); payment of nonrefundable application fee.

Applicant must be licensed in good standing in a state with substantially equivalent requirements, have no final or pending disciplinary action, have graduated from a CODA-accredited school, passed a recognized national or other exam, passed the jurisprudence exam, submitted current CPR certification, practiced for at least 3 years preceding application, and been endorsed by the board of dentistry in the jurisdiction where they practice.

Must be currently licensed in good standing with an unrestricted license in another jurisdiction, document having met all requirements for licensure (except the dental school degree requirement), and document having been successfully engaged in clinical practice as a dentist for not less than 6,000 hours in the five years immediately preceding the date of application.

Applicant must meet standard requirements, hold a current unrestricted license in another US jurisdiction in good standing, have not committed acts constituting grounds for denial, and have been in continuous clinical practice for five out of the six years immediately preceding application.

Must be currently licensed in good standing in a US or Canadian jurisdiction with substantially equivalent requirements; complete an approved emergency office procedures course; complete the dentist jurisprudence examination; and meet active practice requirements established by the Board by rule.

Applicant must hold a valid license in another state and either (a) be a graduate of a dental college approved by the commission, or (b) have practiced at least four years in another state AND completed a one-year postdoctoral residency approved by the commission. Commission may also require documentation of licensure and knowledge of Washington law.

Must be licensed in good standing in another state/territory/country, meet requirements established by the examining board by rule, submit evidence of current CPR proficiency, present the license to the examining board, and pay the applicable fee.

Applicant must be currently licensed in at least one other state in the same discipline, license in good standing, previously passed required examinations, and for dentistry professions must have completed a clinical hand-skills exam

Applicant must hold a relevant, active license in good standing from another state with substantially equivalent or more stringent requirements; must demonstrate competency; must not have engaged in acts constituting grounds for refusal/suspension/revocation; must complete all application procedures and pay required fees. Note: W.S. 33-1-120(d)(ii) excludes professions with prescriptive drug authority from this general reciprocity provision, so dentists may be excluded.
